questions.question: Write the word equation for photosynthesis and explain why sunlight and chlorophyll are written at the arrow rather than on the left-hand side.
questions.expected_answer: Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, with sunlight and chlorophyll as conditions at the arrow. Carbon dioxide and water are raw materials that are used up; sunlight is the energy source and chlorophyll the pigment that captures it — neither is consumed as a substance, so they are conditions, not reactants.

questions.question: Describe the starch test on a leaf, giving the purpose of boiling in water, boiling in ethanol, and using a water bath. State the result for a leaf kept in the light and one kept covered.
questions.expected_answer: Boil the leaf in water to kill and soften it so iodine can enter; boil in ethanol to remove chlorophyll so the colour change is visible; the ethanol is heated in a water bath with the flame off because ethanol is highly flammable. Rinse in warm water, spread on a white tile, add iodine. The leaf from the light turns blue-black (starch present, photosynthesis occurred); the covered leaf stays yellow-brown (no starch, no photosynthesis without light). The plant is destarched in the dark for about 48 hours beforehand so any starch found was made during the test.

questions.question: Name four compounds a plant makes from glucose, state the purpose of each, and explain why protein needs something extra from the soil.
questions.expected_answer: Starch — storage (potato, maize); cellulose — structure, cell walls (cotton, paper); sucrose — transport in the phloem (sugar cane); oils/fats — concentrated energy store in seeds (sunflower). Protein contains nitrogen, which glucose lacks, so the plant must absorb nitrates (mineral salts) dissolved in soil water and combine them with carbon compounds from glucose.
